title: Egg Omelet with Cheese and Tomatoes

content.title: About
content.content: Egg omelet with cheese and tomatoes is a simple dish made from eggs, grated cheese, and fresh tomatoes. Eggs provide high‑quality protein, cheese adds a creamy flavor and calcium, and tomatoes bring freshness and vitamin C.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most affordable complete protein sources.
Cream cheese is popular in cooking for its smooth texture and neutral taste.
Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
An omelet can be prepared in 5‑7 minutes, making it a favorite breakfast.
Around the world, omelets are customized with herbs, meats, or vegetables.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs contain all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cream cheese contributes calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Vitamin C and lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes provide vitamin C and lycopene, boosting immunity and protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: The dish is suitable for low‑carb diets as it contains minimal sugar.

items.title: Eye health support
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin from eggs and tomatoes help maintain healthy vision.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume the dish in moderation.

items.title: Sodium in cheese
items.content: Cream cheese can be salty, so choose low‑sodium varieties if you watch your salt intake.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked eggs may harbor salmonella; cook until fully set.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the omelet hot, optionally garnish with fresh herbs, add avocado or whole‑grain toast. It works well as a breakfast or a light lunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours and reheat before serving.
